model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Crawford's incumbency and roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge over Terri Green, and market pricing near 97% Republican all point the same direction, with no evidence on the other side to move the forecast.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Crawford or a major scandal could narrow the margin, though nothing of the kind is currently visible.

overview:
Rick Crawford seeks another term in a northeastern Arkansas district with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward Republicans. Renominated without difficulty, he enters the general election with a commanding financial edge: about $1.1 million raised and $875,000 on hand, against roughly $112,000 raised and under $6,000 remaining for Democrat Terri Green. Libertarian Steve Parsons also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 1%. The combination of the seat's strong Republican tilt, Crawford's incumbency, and the wide money gap makes an upset highly unlikely in a contest that has attracted little outside attention or spending.
